A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GM-RBM research. All pages, equations, figures, tables, and references are readable and support comparison. Neither PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original word-pair recall experiments in Figures 1–2 and GM-RBM-generated MNIST and CelebA samples in Figure 3.

after.justification: v2 retains the original recall experiments and reports generated images plus a new quantitative FID comparison in Table 3.

M1.justification: The core energy, architecture, and Gibbs/contrastive-divergence procedure are retained. v2's abstract newly mentions temperature annealing and intra-slot diversity constraints, but neither is specified in the methods or experimental settings. Whether these represent actual procedural additions remains unresolved.

E1.justification: Reported evaluations remain WordNet-based word-pair recall and MNIST/CelebA image generation. The new FID evaluation stays within existing image-generation coverage; other modalities remain proposed future work.

E2.justification: GB-RBM using Gibbs–Langevin remains the comparator for recall and image generation. The new FID table uses this existing baseline and additional q configurations of GM-RBM; no distinct comparison method is introduced.

E3.justification: v2 adds FID evaluation across q = 2, 4, 6, reporting fixed negative-phase budgets and capacity matching through m' ≈ m log2(q). Existing recall settings and Table 2 training budgets are retained. The added protocol is inconsistently described: Table 3 says parameter-matched, whereas Section 5.2.1 says capacity-matched.

E4.justification: The recall q and hidden-unit sweeps are retained. New Table 3 adds an image-quality sensitivity analysis across q = 2, 4, 6. The additional sampler ablations proposed in Section 6.1 have no reported outcomes.

E5.justification: Both versions describe independently trained recall markers and explicitly omit error bars. The added FID scores also lack repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No new uncertainty-reporting practice is demonstrated.

E6.justification: Previously qualitative image-generation evidence gains a quantitative comparison: Table 3 reports FID 67.08, 56.09, and 53.07 for GM-RBM q = 2, 4, and 6, versus 60.06 for GB-RBM. Figure 3b replaces the CelebA examples. Recall plots and MNIST samples remain unchanged. These are added or replaced results, not established same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: v2 substantially expands the formal treatment with explicit hidden softmax conditionals, the completed-square constant, a q = 2 reduction, parameter counts, likelihood-gradient expressions, and Langevin update analysis. The original energy and Gaussian visible conditional remain. v1's separate DBM-front-end energy, Equation 7, is omitted.

C1.justification: The central architectural contribution remains. v2 qualifies the abstract's outperformance claim as competitive or improved recall in several equal-capacity regimes, and promotes matching protocols and equal-budget FID trends to explicit contributions. It also newly claims anti-collapse training without documenting it in the body.

C2.justification: v1 treats the absence of Langevin sampling as a limitation on potential mixing and sample-quality gains; v2 presents pure Gibbs as an intentional advantage and argues that Langevin refinement is unnecessary. It adds a mixing-based interpretation of CelebA FID and specific uncertainties concerning embedding robustness, retrieval degradation, and deeper architectures.

D1.justification: Section 3.5 newly specifies per-slot softmax sampling and a single exact Gaussian visible draw without step-size tuning. Existing hardware, preprocessing, optimizer settings, and epoch budgets are retained. The promised annealing/diversity settings, sampler step counts, persistence details, and sampling diagnostics are not supplied.

R1.justification: v2 removes the introduction's detailed comparisons with mixed-variate RBMs, texture RBMs, implicit RBM mixtures, and auxiliary-variable energy models, alongside numerous related references. It adds Smolensky and Heusel et al. Positioning shifts substantially toward matching protocols and sampling efficiency.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background, theoretical exposition, and limitations are extensively rewritten and reorganized. Experimental-setup subsections are consolidated, training becomes a separate subsection, and several broader-impact subsections are condensed. Mohamed Elfouly is added to the author list.

P2.justification: A different document template changes margins, typography, title and author arrangement, and table styling throughout. Figures 1–2 are enlarged and relocated. Figure 3b changes from a noise-to-face progression to a larger face gallery, and Table 3 adds the FID display.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful mathematical detail, quantitative image-quality evidence, and more specific limitations. However, Section 3.4 and Table 3/Section 5.2.1 inconsistently define the matching protocol, while newly claimed annealing/diversity details and sampling diagnostics are absent. These problems affect the interpretation and reproducibility of the main additions, preventing a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
